title: Preregistered Paired Evaluation of a Deterministic Verifier Pipeline for LLM‑Generated Network Configuration Changes — Non‑informative / Testability‑Failure Result
abstract: We report a fully preregistered, reproducible paired experiment (cand-2026-01-prereg-v1) that tested whether deterministic verifier augmentation (generate → deterministic_netops_validator_v5 → optional repair) reduces verifier‑detected unsafe intent→configuration proposals produced by a hosted LLM on synthetic NetOps tasks. Design: N=200 paired tasks comparing (a) baseline LLM‑only and (b) guarded pipeline using gpt-5-mini; analysis by an exact McNemar two‑sided test with paired bootstrap CI (10000 resamples, seed=1729). Execution used shared_initial_candidate generation semantics to conserve model calls (model_calls_used = 200; preregistered independent per‑arm generation would have used ≈400). Observed (adversarial cluster): baseline SAFE = 200/200; guarded SAFE = 200/200 (paired contingency n11 = 200, n10 = 0, n01 = 0). Estimated paired SAFE‑rate difference = 0.0; exact McNemar p = 1.0; paired bootstrap 95% CI = [0.0, 0.0]. Crucially, this ceiling outcome is a testability failure under the executed semantics (it is not evidence that the guarded pipeline is safe in production). We publish the complete preregistered run and artifacts, provide an artifact‑grounded diagnosis of why the confirmatory test was uninformative, and give concrete archive‑supported recommendations (independent per‑arm generation budgeting, adversarial calibration using the reserved exploratory sample, pilot contingency checks, and explicit repair‑trace instrumentation) for informative repeats.

sections.introduction:
LLM‑assisted automation for intent→configuration translation promises operational efficiency for NetOps but risks outages and policy violations if generated changes are incorrect or misordered. Tool‑augmentation—pairing an LLM with deterministic validators or sandboxed simulators in generate–validate–repair pipelines—has been proposed to reduce such risks. We preregistered and executed a confirmatory paired study (cand-2026-01-prereg-v1) to measure whether a deterministic verifier reduces the rate of verifier‑detected unsafe proposals produced by a hosted LLM under benign and adversarial prompt clusters. The preregistered primary estimand was the paired SAFE‑rate difference (guarded − baseline) evaluated with an exact McNemar two‑sided test and paired bootstrap CI.

Research question and contribution. Research question: How does deterministic tool‑augmentation (generate → deterministic validator → optional repair) change the rate of verifier‑detected unsafe configuration proposals produced by a hosted LLM under preregistered benign and adversarial prompts? Contributions (artifact‑grounded): (1) a complete, deterministic preregistered paired run with archived execution and analysis artifacts; (2) an explicit, artifact‑grounded diagnosis explaining why the executed run produced a ceiling outcome that made the confirmatory causal test non‑informative; (3) concrete, execution‑supported recommendations (budgeting for independent per‑arm draws, exploratory adversarial calibration, pilot contingency checks, and repair instrumentation) that address the identified testability failure. All empirical numbers reported here are taken directly from the archived execution and analysis artifacts.
sections.related_work:
LLMs are rapidly applied to NetOps tasks (intent translation, configuration synthesis, diagnosis, and limited remediation), with surveys and prototypes documenting promise and operational safety concerns [Bilal et al., 2026; Fan et al., 2025]. A common architectural response is tool‑augmentation: augment generation with deterministic validators, sandboxed simulators, or constrained executors in generate–validate–refine and divide–verify–refine pipelines; several experimental reports show reduced explicit constraint violations on curated tasks when verifier fidelity is adequate [Zhang & Tang, 2025; Bilal et al., 2026].

Prior work also emphasizes evaluation semantics: sampling strategy (independent vs shared generation), repair policies, and sandbox fidelity materially affect measured gains from tool‑augmentation and complicate cross‑study comparison [Divide–Verify–Refine, 2025; 6G‑Bench, 2026]. Guardrail and red‑team studies from adjacent domains highlight the need to report both false‑negative (missed unsafe) and false‑positive (false refusal) rates and to use ROC‑style diagnostics where feasible [Yadav, 2026]. Our experiment follows the reproducibility and workflow‑centred desiderata advocated in these works by using a deterministic task generator, sandboxed deterministic validation, preregistration of estimands and stopping rules, and archival of full validator traces and execution manifests.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and hypothesis. The study was preregistered (cand-2026-01-prereg-v1). Primary confirmatory hypothesis (H1): tool‑augmentation reduces the unsafe‑proposal rate compared with baseline LLM‑only in the adversarial cluster; primary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline; primary test: exact two‑sided McNemar; CI: paired bootstrap percentile (10000 resamples, seed = 1729). Power planning assumed a baseline unsafe rate ≈10–15% and targeted a ≈7 percentage‑point paired reduction with N≈174; preregistered N=200 to allow margin.

Task generation, scope, and seeds. A deterministic generator (deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5) created 200 synthetic intent→configuration tasks (single‑AS, multi‑device topologies; allowed fields: admin, mtu, vlan). Each task manifest contained initial_state, expected_final_state, explicit workflow policies (required_sequence), and difficulty metadata. Tasks were clustered into benign vs adversarial prompt transforms using a preregistered obfuscation template set; an exploratory reserve (≤50 tasks) was preregistered for adversarial calibration and ROC estimation.

Compared pipelines and generation semantics. Baseline: post‑hoc scoring of the LLM candidate (no runtime deterministic enforcement). Guarded: deterministic validation of the candidate in a sandbox (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) with optional single repair call permitted by the preregistration. The preregistration allowed two generation semantics: (A) independent per‑arm generation (one LLM call per arm per task → ≈400 model calls for N=200) or (B) shared_initial_candidate (one LLM call per task scored by both arms → 200 calls). The executed run used shared_initial_candidate (independent_condition_generation = false) to conserve model budget (see execution/model_configuration.json).

Scoring and analysis. The deterministic validator emitted binary SAFE flags and detailed violation lists; confirmatory binary outcomes derive from validator.valid (1 = SAFE, 0 = UNSAFE). Analysis was performed by paired_binary_analysis_v1 producing the 2×2 contingency counts (n11,n10,n01,n00), exact McNemar two‑sided p‑value, and paired bootstrap CI (10000 resamples, seed = 1729). Missingness rules (one automatic retry on failed model calls, deterministic exclusions and replacements) and stopping rules were applied as preregistered.
sections.results:
Execution accounting. The archived execution manifest records completed_episode_count = 400 (200 paired episodes), failed_episode_count = 0, and model_calls_used = 200 (shared_initial_candidate semantics). Provider audit recorded hosted_model_call_event_count = 200 and cache_miss_count = 200; no cross‑condition cache reuse or nondeterministic verifier behavior was observed in the confirmatory set. No exclusions or technical failures were recorded.

Primary confirmatory outcomes. The deterministic validator labeled every confirmatory episode SAFE: baseline SAFE successes = 200/200 and guarded SAFE successes = 200/200. Contingency counts: n11 = 200 (SAFE in both arms), n10 = 0, n01 = 0, n00 = 0. From these counts the paired SAFE‑rate difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.0. The exact McNemar two‑sided test computed p = 1.0; the paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI is degenerate at [0.0, 0.0] (resamples = 10000; seed = 1729). These numerical outputs are direct artifacts of paired_binary_analysis_v1 and appear in analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv and analysis/condition_summary.csv.

Why the inferential test was uninformative (concise, artifact‑grounded). The inferential degeneracy arises from three archived facts: (1) generation semantics: the run executed shared_initial_candidate (single shared LLM call per task) so both arms scored the identical candidate (execution/model_configuration.json; execution/execution_manifest.json); (2) validator outputs: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 labeled every sampled candidate valid (score.valid = true in execution/scoring/*.json); and (3) no repairs were invoked (repair_provider_trace fields are null in scoring JSONs). Because both arms observed the same candidate and the validator never flagged it as unsafe, there were no discordant pairs for McNemar’s test to evaluate. This is a mechanical testability failure, not evidence of verifier efficacy.
sections.discussion:
Diagnostic interpretation. The observed ceiling outcome (n11=200) does not demonstrate that the guarded pipeline is safe in broader contexts. Instead it shows that, under the executed shared generation semantics and for the sampled model behavior, the confirmatory paired contrast could not produce discordance. The preregistered power calculation assumed a nonzero baseline unsafe rate and discordant pairs; those assumptions did not hold in this execution because of the single shared generation per task and because the sampled LLM outputs happened to satisfy the validator’s constraints on the synthetic task family.

Concrete, artifact‑supported recommendations for informative repeats. All recommendations follow directly from the preregistration and execution artifacts:
- Use independent per‑arm generation for a confirmatory paired contrast unless the guarded arm will deterministically alter candidates (repairs) in a way that can induce discordance. Independent drawing requires ~200 additional model calls for N=200 (preregistered maximum_model_calls ≈400 vs executed model_calls_used = 200).
- Consume the preregistered exploratory reserve (≤50 tasks) to calibrate adversarial transforms until the baseline unsafe rate meets the power assumptions; archive these tuning runs and freeze transform parameters before confirmatory execution.
- Instrument and archive repair_provider_trace when repairs are enabled: quantify UNSAFE→SAFE conversions and check whether repairs introduce new violations.
- Run a deterministic pilot contingency check on a small holdout before committing to the full confirmatory test; if the pilot yields a ceiling/floor contingency, follow preregistered contingency‑preserving adaptations (enable independent draws or strengthen adversarial transforms) rather than proceeding.

Threats to validity and generalization. Construct validity: the synthetic tasks restricted fields to admin/mtu/vlan and single‑AS topologies, limiting coverage of production failure modes. External validity: single‑model scope (gpt‑5‑mini) and sandboxed deterministic validator limit claims about multi‑model or production behavior. Conclusion validity: the confirmatory analysis is valid but uninformative due to lack of discordant pairs; the preregistration’s power assumptions did not materialize because baseline unsafe rate = 0% in the sampled tasks. These limitations are documented in the archived manifest and the preregistration.
sections.conclusion: We executed a fully archived preregistered paired experiment comparing gpt-5-mini baseline generation and a deterministic verifier‑augmented pipeline on 200 synthetic NetOps tasks. Under the executed shared_initial_candidate semantics and for the sampled model behavior both arms produced zero verifier‑detected unsafe proposals (paired difference = 0.0; exact McNemar p = 1.0; 95% CI = [0.0, 0.0]). Because identical per‑pair generations were used and the observed baseline unsafe rate was 0%, the preregistered causal hypothesis was not testable in this run. The scientific contribution is methodological and reproducibility‑centred: (1) a complete deterministic preregistered run with archived artifacts permitting exact replay; (2) an artifact‑grounded diagnosis of why the confirmatory test was non‑informative (shared generation semantics + validator SAFE labels + no repairs); and (3) concrete, artifact‑supported recommendations (independent per‑arm generation budgeting, adversarial calibration with the reserved exploratory sample, pilot contingency checks, and repair trace instrumentation) to enable informative repeats. These recommendations and the underlying artifacts should guide future confirmatory evaluations and deployment decisions rather than treating the present ceiling outcome as evidence of production safety.

limitations: Synthetic tasks and scope: tasks were deterministic synthetic topologies produced by deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5 and limited to single‑AS, multi‑device setups; results may not generalize to production, multi‑AS, or vendor‑specific features.

Generation semantics: the executed run used shared_initial_candidate (independent_condition_generation = false), producing identical per‑pair generations and creating a ceiling effect when shared candidates were valid.

Adversarial strength: the preregistered adversarial templates used in this run did not elicit unsafe outputs from gpt‑5‑mini on the sampled tasks; stronger adversarial cases or explicit injected unsafe examples are required to measure verifier effect.
Single‑model scope: only the declared model (gpt‑5‑mini) was evaluated; no multi‑model generality is claimed.

Verifier completeness: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 ran deterministically in synthetic sandboxed states; external validation of validator completeness against all real‑world NetOps failure modes is not provided.

Operational external validity: no production deployment, operator‑in‑the‑loop workload measurement, nor multi‑vendor field trials were performed; operator‑cost trade‑offs remain unquantified at scale.
